# Class 6 geography, ~2 minutes, written by Claude for F-014 S3 (processes). Expect: a content slide on the water cycle;
# "let me show you the water cycle" opens simulation mode with the four steps drawn and unnamed; each step said moves
# the stage and names it (evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection); transpiration and runoff are drawn
# only once said; "washing machine ... cycle" is a trap; "let's get back to the slides" ends the mode with a recap;
# then the slides go on (groundwater). No numbers anywhere: nothing printed but the step names said.
@setup subject=Geography grade=6 topic="The water cycle"

Good morning everyone. Today we will learn about the water cycle.
[pause 1]
Water on the earth keeps moving between the sea, the air and the land. This movement never stops.
It is powered by the heat of the sun.
[pause 1.5]
Let me show you the water cycle.
First, the sun heats the water in the oceans, lakes and rivers, and the water evaporates into water vapour.
Plants also lose water from their leaves into the air. We call this transpiration.
[pause 1]
As the water vapour rises, it cools and condenses into tiny droplets, and these droplets form clouds.
When the droplets join together and become heavy, they fall back to the earth as rain, snow or hail. This is precipitation.
[pause 1]
Some of the rain flows over the ground into rivers. That is called runoff.
Finally the water collects in the oceans and lakes, and the whole cycle starts again.
[pause 1.5]
Think about it: a washing machine also runs a rinse cycle with water, but that is not a natural cycle.
The water cycle has no beginning and no end.
[pause 1]
Okay, let's get back to the slides.
[pause 1]
Some rain water also seeps into the soil and becomes groundwater.
Groundwater is stored in rocks called aquifers, and we draw it up with wells.
